newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries ease in London, downside seen limited.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries ease in London, downside seen limited.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries dipped on profit taking in London on Friday, but analysts said the downside was limited given receding speculation of a U.S. rate rise.
"I wouldn't want to get carried away on the downside. I would regard it essentially as profit taking," said Michael Hughes, bond trader at Barclays de Zoete Wedd in London.
A flood of dollar Eurobond issues competing for investor money has put a dampener on Treasuries, but the market is underpinned by cuts in U.S. supply, traders said.

By 1000 GMT, the long bond was quoted at 99-04, yielding 6.69 percent, compared with 99-06 in Tokyo and 99-09 at the New York close. The two-year note traded at 100-13, yielding 6.02 percent, unchanged from Tokyo and against 100-14 in New York.
"The interest is really in the 10-year plus," said Hughes, adding short end yields were at their bottom after discounting for this week's mostly soft economic data.
"For that six percent (on two-year) to break you're actually talking about a favourable environment where rates don't have to go up at all," he added.
On Thursday, a sharp rise in weekly jobless data gave a lift to Treasuries but the Philadelphia Federal Reserve survey of business conditions came in much higher than forecast.
Bond analysts said even the 10-year sector could have hit a wall with technical charts signalling overbought.
Michael Derks, fixed income strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London, said the 10-year bond did not provide sufficient compensation for a possible rate hike beyond July.
"The problem is there is very little investment value in Treasuries at the moment," Derks said. "You're getting just a 90-basis point pick-up for investing in 10-year over and above Fed funds."
Hughes expected Treasury yields to stick to the 6.0-7.0 percent range for the time being.
"The economy is on a path to slow down on the basis of the interest rate changes already seen and expected and nothing beyond what the forward yield curve has got should be necessary," Hughes said.

No significant data was expected on Friday and analysts said they saw little impact from the G7 meeting over the weekend. Next week, durable goods on Wednesday may provide fresh impetus to the market, analysts said.
Derks said the Tankan survey, the Bank of Japan's quarterly survey of corporate sentiment, on June 25 could be expected to be friendly for Treasuries.
The September T-bond futures were 2/32 down on the day at 112-04 in automated trade.
